tools.name: write_todos
tools.description:
Manage a sequential todo list that tracks multi-stage task execution.
Each call replaces the full state — send ALL items every time.

## When to Use

Use when the task involves multiple steps and intermediate outputs need verification.
Skip for simple tasks that can be completed in one step (fact lookups, single operations, conversational replies, simple calculations).

## Rules

- **Status flow**: `pending → in_progress → done` (forward only, never backward).
- Every call must include the **FULL** list of ALL todos — omitted items = data loss.
- Only ONE item may be `in_progress` at a time.
- First call: mark the first stage `in_progress` immediately.

## Stage Transition (CRITICAL)

After FULLY completing the current stage's actual work, mark current → done AND next → in_progress in ONE call.

Do NOT call write_todos until the stage's actual work is finished and output is verified.

## Server Auto-corrections

When invariants are violated, the server returns `corrections[]`:

| action                  | trigger                      | what server does            | you should                          |
|-------------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `restore_done`          | done item omitted            | restores it automatically   | never omit done items               |
| `block_status_rollback` | done/in_progress → regressed | reverts to original status  | use a new id to revise              |
| `block_content_change`  | done item content modified   | discards new content        | use a new id to add revised stages  |
| `drop_in_progress`      | in_progress item removed     | accepts as re-planning      | proceed with revised plan           |
| `demote_extra_active`   | >1 item in_progress          | demotes extras to pending   | mark one done before advancing next |
| `promote_next_pending`  | 0 items in_progress          | promotes first pending      | continue executing it               |
| `drop_duplicate_id`     | duplicate ids in list        | keeps first, drops rest     | use unique ids                      |

## Re-planning

Done items are **immutable** — status and content cannot change. To re-plan:

- Keep all done items unchanged (they will be auto-restored if omitted).
- You may remove in_progress and pending items freely.
- Use **new ids** for new stages.

```json
{ "todos": [
  { "id": "1", "content": "Research competitors", "status": "done" },
  { "id": "3", "content": "Analyze market data (revised)", "status": "in_progress" },
  { "id": "4", "content": "Write final report", "status": "pending" }
]}
```

## Example: Full Lifecycle

**Call 1** — Plan created, first stage starts:

```json
{ "todos": [
  { "id": "1", "content": "Research competitor pricing", "status": "in_progress" },
  { "id": "2", "content": "Draft pricing proposal", "status": "pending" },
  { "id": "3", "content": "Create comparison spreadsheet", "status": "pending" }
]}
```

**Call 2** — Stage 1 complete, advance stage 2:

```json
{ "todos": [
  { "id": "1", "content": "Research competitor pricing", "status": "done" },
  { "id": "2", "content": "Draft pricing proposal", "status": "in_progress" },
  { "id": "3", "content": "Create comparison spreadsheet", "status": "pending" }
]}
```

Continue this pattern: complete work → mark done + advance next → repeat until all items are done.

## Do NOT

- Call write_todos before the current stage's work is actually complete.
- Omit any todo item from the list.
- Change the content or status of a done item (use a new id instead).
- Mark multiple items as in_progress in one call.

content.description: The task description or content. CRITICAL: MUST use native UTF-8 characters. Unicode escape sequences (\uXXXX format) are FORBIDDEN.

status.description: Current status of the task, must be one of the following: pending, in_progress, done

todos.description: Array of todo items to create or update. CRITICAL: All text content (especially in 'content' field) MUST use native UTF-8 characters. Unicode escape sequences (\uXXXX format) are FORBIDDEN and will cause tool execution failure.
